title: Wage judgments, wage cases and labor debarments against firms doing public work
question: Do firms with a wage judgment, a prevailing-wage finding or a labor debarment keep getting work from the City or from other public bodies?
finding: 462 Labor Commissioner judgments against San Francisco employers, 451 federal wage cases in the Bay Area closed since 2015 (those on government contracts, or with $10,000 or more of back wages), 295 State prevailing-wage decisions and 57 State public-works debarments were set against City payees, contract teams, the other public bodies' contractors and the bid sheets. 14 judgments, 19 federal cases, 6 State decisions and 0 State debarments match a name; 19 of the 39 matches are confirmed by the same street address. 4 of the matches (two firms) are contractors of another public body; none is a bidder on the bid sheets. The most recent case on public work: Mark Scott Construction, Inc., 3 federal cases with findings periods from October 2024 to May 2025, $74,354 of back wages under the federal construction-wage law; the City paid the firm $6.4 million since fiscal 2019, last in fiscal 2026, almost all before those cases. No firm with a State debarment or a recent prevailing-wage finding is shown winning new City work afterwards.
how: Four enforcement lists are matched by exact normalised name (registered name and trade name) to City payees paid $10,000 or more since fiscal 2019, to every contract-team member, to the contractors in the other public bodies' board items and to the bidders on 108 bid sheets. The address on the judgment or federal case is then compared with the addresses the Treasurer's registry and the State licence file hold for that name. This extends the planning_records screen, which matched the judgments to City payees by name only.
limits: A wage judgment or a federal back-wage finding is usually about a few workers and often about private work; the State search warns that payments made directly to workers are not always recorded, so "open" may be paid. Federal Service Contract Act cases concern federal contracts, not City ones. The State decisions list and the debarment list carry no addresses, so matches there cannot be confirmed from these files. The full State register of public-works projects and contractors is not on disk.
